source: <color=#FDBCA4>G</color><size=18>REAT,</size> <color=#FDBCA4>W</color><size=18>ONDERFUL,</size> <color=#FDBCA4>A</color><size=18>NCIENT</size>
target: <color=#FDBCA4>偉</color><size=18>大、</size><color=#FDBCA4>奇</color><size=18>妙、</size><color=#FDBCA4>古</color><size=18>老的</size>

source: SPIRITS
target: 靈魂

source: Oh Great Spirit Unetlanvhi, Oh ancient Beloved Unega Long Spirit, I seek strength… not to live But to die with clean hands and straight eyes, Without fear… so my spirit May meet you without shame. Protect brother kvtli… raccoon with coat White and pure as mountain snow. It is with honor I freed him From the trap that sna— Snaps like cougar’s jaw, Hidden in the creek waters for brother beaver By the evil pale tricksters Who kill… with glee. It is— It is with honor I take their punishment. Proudly I lay dying… Pierced in the stomach by a stone Shot from their loud… st-sticks of evil magic. Let them track me to this cave. Let them – ah – take my skin, dirty and bloody. I accept the path of my star I c-cannot see. May frustration rot their hearts. For br-brother raccoon With his fur as p-perfect as clouds… Shall never… Be… Theirs.
target: 噢，偉大之靈Unetlanvhi， 噢，古老摯愛的白色長靈Unega， 我尋求力量……並非求生， 而是以乾淨雙手、坦然目光死去， 不帶恐懼……讓靈魂 與祢相見時，無須羞愧。 保護kvtli兄弟……浣熊， 皮毛如山雪般純白。 我光榮地釋放牠， 掙脫那啪—— 像美洲獅顎般咬合的陷阱， 邪惡蒼白的騙子 將它藏在溪水裡，捕捉河狸兄弟。 他們殺戮……歡喜地殺。 這是—— 我光榮地承受他們的懲罰。 驕傲地躺著，將死…… 肚腹被石頭穿透， 從他們巨響的……邪術棍射出。 任他們追我到洞穴。 任他們——啊——取走骯髒染血的皮。 我接受那顆星的道路， 那我看、看不見的道路。 願挫敗腐蝕他們的心。 因為浣、浣熊兄弟， 皮毛如雲般完、完美…… 永遠不會…… 屬於…… 他們。

source: Spearfinger : Aah-ah-aaahh!
Spearfinger : Ah-ah-ahhh!
target: 矛指：啊、啊、啊！

source: Spearfinger : Eee-eee-eee!
target: 矛指：咿、咿、咿！

source: When the young warriors toil with making spirit shields, then it is certain: a great fear has invaded our people. First there was a sighting by the children. “U'tlun'ta'!” they cried, “It is Spearfinger!” They clung to my robe and flitted around me like startled chickadees. Who told them about this legend, this witch with a dress of stone and a sharp finger for cutting out livers to eat? I had thought it was our scamp kanohetlvsgi, our old storyteller, giving the young ones a fright by saying that the hungry witch lurks in our woods. He denied this. But he denies much. Then Ostenaco, Big Head, the most serious young man, woke me suddenly in the afternoon six moons ago. He said Spearfinger approached him and his friends who were fishing in the red stream. They ran at the sight of a strange woman in a dress that shone like wet stone in sunlight, her left hand bearing a claw-like finger. That was the first time I heard his voice shake. And two mornings ago Immokalee, Tumbling Water, aged but thirteen harvests, was found dead by the same red stream. Little neck snapped. Pouch of mulberries spilled. Tracks leading away from her body. A great fear has taken us. I know what I must do. It will take all my strength.
target: 當年輕戰士忙著製作靈盾，便能確定：巨大的恐懼已侵入族人。 最先看見的是孩子。 「U'tlun'ta'！」他們哭喊，「是矛指！」抓著我的袍子，像受驚山雀般繞著我。誰告訴他們這傳說？那個穿石衣、以尖指挖肝來吃的女巫？ 我以為是我們頑皮的kanohetlvsgi，老說書人，說飢餓女巫藏在樹林，嚇唬孩子。他否認，可他什麼都否認。 接著，六個月前的午後，最嚴肅的年輕人Ostenaco，大頭，突然叫醒我。他說，他和朋友在紅溪釣魚，矛指走近。他們看見一個奇怪女人，衣服如陽光下的濕石般發亮，左手有爪般的長指，立刻逃跑。那是我第一次聽見他聲音顫抖。 兩個早晨前，才經歷十三次收穫的Immokalee，翻騰之水，被發現死在同一條紅溪旁。小小脖子折斷，袋裡桑葚散落。腳印從屍體旁離去。 巨大的恐懼攫住我們。我知道必須做什麼。 這將耗盡我的力量。

source: Hour 1: I comb my wrinkled arms slow and hard until skin breaks and releases Uyoi Gigv, Unclean Blood. I am red and new like the dawn. Hour 3: My body regains life and strength in the cool flowing steam. I take seven plunges each time reborn in water, in wind. Hour 10: I crest our mountain Ulogili Ukadv – Cloudy Face and imbibe Black Drink of Yaupon holly that purges my insides until all is nothing but pure. Hour 12: I burn tobacco for its silver smoke carries my song of protection To Unetlanvhi. I dance and sing until my spirit, adanvdo, is freed from this body. My adanvdo shall strengthen honorable ghosts and protect from Spearfinger, witches, and evils through all suns and moons the People living among the pines. So I sing: BLESS THE RAIN THAT HELPS US GROW BLESS THE WIND THAT BRINGS REBIRTH BLESS RACCOON WHO TENDS TIME’S FLOW BLESS THE PEOPLE OF PINE’S EARTH ADADOLISDI ITSU-LA-A-YV
target: 第一個時辰： 我緩慢用力梳刮皺臂， 直到皮開，流出 Uyoi Gigv，不潔之血。 我鮮紅而新生， 如黎明。 第三個時辰： 身體在清涼流水裡， 重獲生命與力量。 我七度潛入， 每次重生， 在水中，在風中。 第十個時辰： 登上我們的山Ulogili Ukadv——雲面， 飲下由冬青製成的黑飲， 淨空內裡， 直到一切只剩 純潔。 第十二個時辰： 燃燒菸草，讓銀煙 承載守護之歌， 獻予Unetlanvhi。 我舞，我唱， 直到靈魂adanvdo， 脫離此身。 我的adanvdo將壯大榮耀的亡靈， 於每個日月， 保護松林中的族人， 遠離矛指、女巫與邪惡。 所以我唱： 祝福助我成長的雨， 祝福帶來重生的風， 祝福照料時流的浣熊， 祝福松林大地的族人。 ADADOLISDI ITSU-LA-A-YV

source: GREAT BLESSING OF PROTECTION FOR THE PEOPLE OF THE PINES
target: 賜予松林族人的偉大守護祝福

source: There! A hint of it. Damp. A damp pocket in the cool soil. Ah, how refreshing to soak this little patch. Ever since my seed sprouted in a sudden downpour four seasons ago, life has been nothing but exhausting focus. All my energy and concentration goes into growing my tap root. Reaching, reaching through cracks and crevices in this hard earth, reaching down and bending and reaching to feel the slightest touch of luscious wetness sleeping in the ground. A touch is often enough for another day of growth. Were it not for the lucky path of my tap root, the heat and dust of this world would soon shrivel me dead. I see the humans loping through the heat between the pine forest and their village. I feel like I know the expression they wear. Anxious and focused. Reaching for a touch of sustenance. To survive one more day.
target: 那裡！一絲痕跡。濕氣。 涼土裡一小團濕潤。啊，吸飽這一小片，多麼清爽。 四季前，種子在突如其來的暴雨裡發芽。此後生命全是耗人的專注。所有能量與心力，都用來長主根。伸，伸過硬土裂隙，向下，彎曲，再伸，尋找沉睡地底、甘美濕潤最輕微的觸碰。一點點，往往就夠再長一天。 若非主根幸運地找對路，這世界的酷熱塵土，早把我乾死。 我看著人類頂著熱，往返松林與村落。我似乎懂他們的神情，焦慮而專注。伸手尋找一點滋養，好再活一天。

source: Obark Girl: Why dids the cloud come?
target: 歐巴克女孩：雲為什麼來？

source: Obark Boy: But Hero B’zulo and Mama say lost people is tryin’ to kills us…
target: 歐巴克男孩：可布祖洛英雄跟媽媽說，迷路的人想殺我們……

source: Nav’ed Praetis: Very good! So then, the black clouds made everything hot and dry and caused all the dust around us. The snails and people lost a lot of food, so many people left to find clean water. Fortunately, my friends and I had knowledge from past people. We used that knowledge to dig a well right in the middle of the Ringfort, which used to be known as the Judgement… well, nevermind what it used to be. The Ringfort was able to protect the well from violent invaders and dust storms. Its water gave us strength, and we used more knowledge to make small farms of peas and gourds. The food lets us grow, and even lets us take in friendly people who are lost.
target: 納維德・普雷蒂斯：很好！黑雲讓一切又熱又乾，造成四周的塵土。蝸牛和人失去許多食物，所以很多人離開，尋找乾淨水。幸好，我和朋友擁有過去人們的知識。我們靠它，在環堡中央挖井。那裡以前叫審判……算了，從前叫什麼不重要。 環堡能保護水井，抵擋暴力入侵者和沙塵暴。井水給我們力量，再運用更多知識，種出豌豆與葫蘆小田。食物讓我們成長，甚至能收留友善的迷途者。

source: Obark Boy: A weed we gotsta pull?
target: 歐巴克男孩：得拔掉的雜草？

source: Obark Children: AZAAY! AZAAY FOR WATER!
target: 歐巴克孩子們：阿賽！為水歡呼，阿賽！

source: Nav’ed Praetis: Yes, we can! This baby tree showed us that if we dig right around here, we will find water in the ground. Now the village can have a second well!
target: 納維德・普雷蒂斯：能，我們也能喝！這棵小樹告訴我們，在這附近挖，就能找到地下水。村子可以有第二口井了！

source: Nav’ed Praetis: Never forget, little ones – knowledge is what helps us grow. Knowledge found this well! Say, do you want to hear a story about how this village grew?
target: 納維德・普雷蒂斯：孩子們，永遠記住，知識幫助我們成長。是知識找到這口井！想聽村子怎麼長大的故事嗎？

source: Nav’ed Praetis: Water was part of it, yes. Many years ago, before you were born, our village used to be a city with snails the size of huts! But it all crumbled from a big war, and soon after, a great black cloud covered the sky like a mask. It made the air sour, the waters dirty, and caused great heat and drying across the land.
target: 納維德・普雷蒂斯：對，水是其中一部分。很多年前，你們還沒出生，村子原本是座城市，有房子那麼大的蝸牛！後來大戰毀了一切。不久，巨大的黑雲像面具遮住天空，空氣酸嗆，水變髒，整片大地炎熱乾燥。

source: Obark Boy: Water!
target: 歐巴克男孩：水！

source: Nav’ed Praetis: Ah, it’s only a weed until we get to know it. This is a beautiful find. It’s the thriving shoot of a Mesquite Tree. They grow a long, long root, longer than my whole body! And the root reaches down and finds water deep in the ground so the tree can drink and get big!
target: 納維德・普雷蒂斯：啊，不認識它之前，才叫雜草。這是美好的發現，一株茁壯的牧豆樹苗。它的根長得很長，比我整個人還長！深入地下找水，樹才能喝水、長大。

source: Nav’ed Praetis: Look at this plant, little ones.
target: 納維德・普雷蒂斯：孩子們，看看這株植物。

source: Obark Girl: Can we drinks too?
target: 歐巴克女孩：我們也能喝嗎？

source: Nav’ed Praetis: Well, my friends and I believe that far away a great fiery mountain exploded its top off. Ash spewed out and covered our sky. But that is just our “theory.” “Theory” means a very smart guess.
target: 納維德・普雷蒂斯：我和朋友認為，遠方一座巨大火山炸開山頂，噴出灰，遮住天空。不過，這只是我們的「理論」。「理論」就是很聰明的猜想。

source: Obark Children: THEERY! THEERY!
target: 歐巴克孩子們：理——論！理——論！

source: Quentinite Kelyn: Give it time. This idea… this project is the best we can do right now. Your imagination gives us a chance. Who else would know to breed roadrunners, which can travel up to 100 miles a day, and then send them out in all directions with simple maps of our region and waterholes?
target: 昆汀修士凱琳：給它時間。這想法、這計畫，已是目前能做最好的事。你的想像力給了我們機會。還有誰會想到繁育走鵑，這種一天能走一百英里的鳥，再讓牠們帶著地區與水源簡圖，奔向四方？

source: Quentinite Kelyn: My dear husband, you know what will help? Listen to this old poem by an ancient scribe called Emily Dickinson. I memorized this one quickly. It’s beauty is treasure. Listen now: ‘Hope’ is the thing with feathers That perches in the soul And sings the tune without the words And never stops at all….
target: 昆汀修士凱琳：親愛的丈夫，知道什麼有幫助嗎？聽聽古代文人艾蜜莉・狄金森的詩。我很快就背下這首，美得如寶藏。聽： 「希望」是有羽毛的東西， 棲息靈魂中， 唱著沒有歌詞的旋律， 從不停止， 一刻也不……

source: Nav’ed Praetis: The source maps must be correct. Definitely correct. Grandfather Fungaki was an incredible cartographer. Maybe hawks and coyotes are killing the birds? Am I just sending them to die?
target: 納維德・普雷蒂斯：原圖一定對，絕對。芬加奇祖父是了不起的製圖師。也許鷹和郊狼殺了鳥？難道我只是送牠們去死？

source: Nav’ed Praetis: Did I miss something? I built the aviary nearly a year ago and no travelers have been able to find us.
target: 納維德・普雷蒂斯：我漏了什麼嗎？鳥舍快建了一年，還沒有旅人找到我們。

source: Quentinite Kelyn: Nav! Enough chewing your nails. The maps will work. Here, eat, husband. The squash stew is sweetened nicely with the pine sap. We can thank Sister Poleeda for that – her winter solstice gift to us, remember?
target: 昆汀修士凱琳：納維！別咬指甲了。地圖會有用。來，吃吧，丈夫。南瓜湯加了松樹液，甜得剛好。得謝謝波莉妲姊妹，那是她送我們的冬至禮物，記得嗎？

source: I thunk we was gonn’ die! Them Obark warriors looked real fearsome, yellin’ and whoopin’ as they come runnin’ at us. Ole Gerrik showed they leader the map we got, ‘splained it was off a roadrunner we trapped durin’ our wanderin’ and so we got led to this village. Oh I was scared somethin’ big. A few old folk thunk we was bein’ bated like dust rabbits to a bushtrap. Sayin’ this Obark tribe could be feastin’ on weak travelers. We all was real hunger-weak from fleein’ our village, now a full moon-path away. Fleein’ from the worst kind of men. The kind who eat other men. Thank all the gods we was wrong. Some people in grey robes come just after the warriors, and one of ‘em was real happy we had the map. He spoke clean like a book, says we done good with followin’ his path. Them robed people – Quent-somethin’s – all was nice like that and gave us water. Warriors scrambled through our supply sledge and took our knives and spears and such. One of the robed people gasped when she saw a couple sweet taters tumble out. She called herself a “bot-and-ist” and was ‘splainin that she gonn' make this little spud feed us good for a long time. Din’t make sense much, but the mean-lookin’ leader and his warriors seemed to calm down after that.
target: 我以為要死啦！歐巴克戰士看著真嚇人，吼著叫著朝我們跑來。 老蓋瑞克給頭領看地圖，說是流浪時抓到一隻走鵑，從牠身上拿到，才找到這村子。 噢，我怕得要命。幾個老人以為，咱們像塵兔被餌引進灌木陷阱。說這歐巴克部落，可能拿虛弱旅人當大餐。我們逃離村子，已走了整整一輪月，全餓得沒力。逃離最壞的那種人，吃人的人。 謝天謝地，我們錯了。戰士後面來了些灰袍人，一個看見地圖，特別高興。說話清楚得像書，說我們循他的路來，做得好。那些袍子人，昆什麼的，全這麼友善，給我們水。 戰士翻我們的物資橇，拿走刀、矛那些東西。幾顆地瓜滾出來，一個袍子女人倒抽氣，說自己是「植、物、學家」，解釋這小薯塊，能讓我們好好吃很久。 不太聽得懂，可兇巴巴的頭領和戰士，似乎就此平靜了。

source:
I greet the usuals as they visit the well:

Hello tall boy with the wild black hair. 

Hello old woman who whistles through her teeth. 

Hello girl who yelps down the well to hear it yelp back. 

Hello old man in the crude gray robes. The one who started it all. 

Hello young man with warrior scars.

Hello mother of little ones who clamber on my limbs. 

Hello short man with very thick haunches.  

Hello, hello, hello. And hello. 

The well: an endless source of water and amusement. Every day, without fail, people of all shapes and ages draw buckets of life out of the ground. Fill their pots and carry them away. Perhaps they stop and chatter, rest in my shade. 

An arid, scorching surface unearthed to meet a wealth of cool, clean sustenance below. 

It took great effort to dig into the hardened earth. Everywhere, it seems, a great effort must be made to find the good.  

If the well were to speak, I think it would agree: most things in life are this way.
target:
常客來井邊，我便招呼：

你好，黑髮亂翹的高男孩。
你好，從牙縫吹口哨的老女人。
你好，對井喊叫、等井回喊的女孩。
你好，穿粗灰袍的老男人，開創一切的人。
你好，帶戰士傷疤的年輕人。
你好，攀爬我枝幹那些小孩的母親。
你好，腿臀粗壯的矮男人。

你好，你好，你好。還有，你好。

水井，無窮的水與樂趣。每天，從不間斷，各種模樣、各種年紀的人，把一桶桶生命從地下拉出，裝滿罐子帶走。也許停下閒聊，在我蔭下歇息。

乾燥灼熱的表層被掘開，接上地底豐富、清涼潔淨的滋養。

挖進硬土，費了很大力氣。似乎到處都一樣，得很努力，才能找到美好。

若水井能說話，我想它會同意：生命中，多數事都如此。
